### 1. Purpose

This document outlines the operational plan for the Summer Reading Challenge 2025 (SRC2025), including target audience, program structure, staffing, resourcing, and key dates. ### 2. Program Overview

The Summer Reading Challenge is the Library Service’s flagship summer program for children and families. It encourages reading engagement during the school holiday period through a structured challenge with rewards, events, and community participation.

**Program Code:** SRC2025  
**Target Audience:** Children aged 5–12 years, with a family engagement component for parents and carers.  
**Program Window:** Summer school holidays (December 2025 – January 2026).

- The mid-challenge reminder SMS, which parents reported helped their children stay on track.

Common suggestions for improvement included:

- A request for a printable list of suggested books for each age group (mentioned in 214 responses).
- A request for more evening events for families where both parents work during the day (mentioned in 168 responses).

The survey also asked respondents to indicate which branch they primarily used. ### 1. Purpose

This document outlines the operational plan for the Summer Reading Challenge 2025 (SRC2025), including target audience, program structure, staffing, resourcing, and key dates. The plan is intended to guide branch coordination and to support the development of promotional materials and partnership agreements.

### 2. Program Overview

The Summer Reading Challenge is the Library Service’s flagship summer program for children and families. It encourages reading engagement during the school holiday period through a structured challenge with rewards, events, and community participation.

**Program Code:** SRC2025  
**Target Audience:** Children aged 5–12 years, with a family engagement component for parents and carers.  
**Program Window:** Summer school holidays (December 2025 – January 2026).

**Start Date:** The Summer Reading Challenge 2025 start_date is set for 2025-12-01 in the program plan. Record status: current. This date is current and confirmed for the official launch across all branches.

---

**1. Executive Summary**

The Summer Reading Challenge 2025 (program code SRC2025) concluded on 31/01/2026. The program was delivered across all six branch libraries and two mobile library stops during the school summer holidays. Final registration data has been reconciled against both the online registration portal and paper sign-on sheets submitted by branch staff.

The Summer Reading Challenge 2025 ran from 01/12/2025 to 31/01/2026, aligning with the Victorian school summer holidays. The program was open to children aged 5–12 years, with a separate young adult track (ages 13–17) offered for the second consecutive year.

**5.1 Digital Literacy for Seniors**

Digital Literacy for Seniors (DLS) provides small-group and one-on-one coaching for older adults. Sessions cover topics including email, online safety, video calling, Medicare and MyGov basics, and using mobile devices. The program runs in eight-week blocks at each branch, with sessions capped at six participants to allow individual attention.

The program report indicates Digital Literacy for Seniors sessions_completed is 24. Record status: current. This figure is current as at the end of the reporting period and includes all scheduled sessions delivered between 01/10/2025 and 31/01/2026. No sessions were cancelled during this period. Two sessions were rescheduled due to facilitator illness in December and were subsequently delivered in the final week of the block.

Attendance remained consistent throughout the block, with a slight dip during the Christmas–New Year period. The Mobile Library routes delivered fewer sessions per route due to travel time between stops; Route A completed three sessions and Route B completed two sessions during the period.

Participant feedback collected at the close of the block (n = 61 responses) indicated:

- 89% of respondents agreed or strongly agreed that they felt more confident using their device after attending sessions.
- 84% reported that they had used the skills learned in sessions at least once per week.
- 77% indicated they would recommend the program to a friend or family member.

The most common topics requested for future blocks were online banking, using telehealth appointments, and understanding scam warning signs.

**5.2 Tech Help Drop-In**

Tech Help Drop-In sessions continue to operate at all static branches. These sessions are not formally structured and do not require booking. Attendees bring their own devices and receive informal assistance from staff or volunteers.

**5.3 Device Lending Pilot**

The device lending pilot commenced 01/11/2025 at Meridian Central and Northgate. The pilot allows registered library members to borrow a Wi-Fi hotspot or a simplified tablet for a three-week loan period. Devices are intended for customers who do not have home internet access or who are considering purchasing a device.

This report provides a detailed breakdown of participation, branch performance, workshop outcomes, and feedback. It also includes a summary of the concurrent Digital Literacy for Seniors program for comparative context, as both programs operated during the same reporting window.

---

**2. Registration and Completion**

Registrations opened on 01/12/2025 and closed on 15/01/2026. Participants could register in person at any branch, via the library website, or through the mobile library routes. Completion was defined as logging at least eight books and submitting the constellation map activity sheet by 31/01/2026.

The completion rate was consistent across branches, with no branch falling below 90%. Mobile Route B recorded the highest completion rate; this route serves two small rural communities where the library staff member reported that the challenge became a shared social activity among families.

---

**3. Books Logged**

A total of 23,412 books were logged by participants during the challenge period. Books were logged through the library's online portal, via paper logs collected at branch desks, and through the mobile library.

Digital Literacy for Seniors total_attendance is 312 according to the program report. Record status: current.

Participants aged 5–8 years logged the highest average number of books at 14.1 per participant. The lowest average was recorded for participants aged 15–17 years at 9.8 books per participant. Anecdotal feedback from branch staff suggests that the older cohort preferred the workshop activities over the reading log component.

---

**4. School-Holiday Workshops**

Forty-nine workshops were delivered during the December 2025 and January 2026 school-holiday periods. All workshops were free to attend, but required booking due to limited capacity.

The reduction is attributed to a lower number of scheduled sessions (49 versus 58 in 2024) rather than a decline in demand. Waitlists for the Constellation Craft and Storytime Under the Stars sessions were reported at all branches.

Northgate recorded the highest proportion of participants aged 5–8 years (38% of their registrants), which aligns with the high average books logged for that age group. Harbourview, the smallest branch, had the highest percentage of Young Adult participants (22%), though their average books logged remained consistent with the overall YA cohort.

Branch staff reported that the reading logs were distributed in paper format at all branches, with a digital version available through the library app. Usage of the digital log was highest at Meridian Central (41% of their participants) and lowest at Harbourview (19%). No branch reported issues with the distribution of physical logs.

---

**6. Completion Rates and Incentives**

Participants were considered to have completed the challenge if they logged at least 12 books and attended at least one library event during the summer period. Table 5 summarises completion rates by age group.

**Table 5: Completion Rates by Age Group**

| Age Group | Registered Participants | Completed Challenge | Completion Rate |

The overall completion rate of 71.5% is an improvement on the 2024 rate of 66.2%. The increase is attributed to the simplified logging process (one book per line rather than one per entry) and the introduction of a mid-challenge reminder SMS to participants who had not logged in the preceding two weeks.

Incentives were distributed as follows:

- 2,766 participants received the completion certificate and a small prize pack (bookmark, sticker sheet, and a voucher for one free children's book from the Friends of the Library bookshop).
- 412 participants who logged more than 20 books received an additional "Super Reader" badge.
- 89 participants who attended five or more events received a "Summer Star" pin.

The prize pack voucher redemption rate was 73.4% as of 28 February 2026. The Friends of the Library reported that the cost of the prize packs was within the agreed budget of $12,000. The Super Reader badges were produced in-house at a cost of $0.85 per badge.

**7. Feedback from Participants and Families**

Feedback was collected through a short online survey distributed to all registered participants' caregivers on 15 January 2026, with a reminder sent on 29 January. A total of 1,847 responses were received, representing a response rate of 47.8% of registered participants. Table 6 summarises the overall satisfaction ratings.

**Table 6: Overall Satisfaction Ratings**

| Question | Very Satisfied | Satisfied | Neutral | Dissatisfied | Very Dissatisfied |
|----------|----------------|-----------|---------|--------------|-------------------|
| Ease of logging books | 61.2% | 29.4% | 6.1% | 2.3% | 1.0% |
| Quality of prize pack | 48.7% | 33.5% | 12.4% | 3.8% | 1.6% |
| Range of library events | 52.3% | 31.9% | 10.2% | 4.1% | 1.5% |
| Communication from library | 44.6% | 36.2% | 13.8% | 3.9% | 1.5% |

The most commonly cited positive aspects of the challenge were:

- The variety of events on offer, particularly the author visits and the Lego building workshops.
- The simplicity of the paper reading log, which several respondents noted was easier for younger children to use than an app.
- The mid-challenge reminder SMS, which parents reported helped their children stay on track.

Common suggestions for improvement included:

- A request for a printable list of suggested books for each age group (mentioned in 214 responses).
- A request for more evening events for families where both parents work during the day (mentioned in 168 responses).
- A request for a separate prize tier for participants who complete the challenge but do not reach the Super Reader threshold (mentioned in 97 responses).

The survey also asked respondents to indicate which branch they primarily used. The distribution of responses by branch was broadly consistent with the distribution of registered participants, with Meridian Central and Eastside each contributing approximately 28% of responses, followed by Northgate (19%), Harbourview (15%), and Westfield (10%).

**8. Events Delivered**

A total of 143 events were delivered across all branches during the summer period, an increase from 128 events in 2024. Table 7 provides a breakdown of events by type.

**Table 7: Events by Type**

| Event Type | Number of Sessions | Total Attendance |
|------------|--------------------|------------------|
| Author and illustrator visits | 12 | 1,204 |
| Storytime and rhyme time | 38 | 2,871 |
| Craft and maker activities | 31 | 1,958 |
| Lego building workshops | 22 | 1,473 |
| Junior book clubs (5–8 years) | 18 | 612 |
| Teen book clubs (13–17 years) | 14 | 403 |
| Family movie screenings | 8 | 1,105 |
| **Total** | **143** | **9,626** |

Attendance at events was recorded by branch staff at the door. A small number of events (7 in total) had attendance recorded as estimates rather than exact counts, where a large walk-in crowd made an exact count impractical; these are flagged in the branch-level event logs.

The author and illustrator visits were the most heavily attended events, with an average attendance of 100 per session. The most popular single event was the visit by children's author Miranda Chen at Meridian Central on 16 January, which attracted 187 attendees and required an overflow room. On the recommendation of branch staff, the library has capped attendance at 150 for future author events to ensure the sessions remain comfortable and interactive.
